key_insight: A hypomorphic founder RAG1 variant caused highly variable immune disease, showing that partial RAG deficiency is shaped by both inherited defect strength and external immune pressures.
clinical_relevance: The multi-omic biomarkers described may help stratify which patients with partial RAG deficiency are progressing and could benefit from closer monitoring or hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
method: Studied 18 Old Order Mennonite individuals with the RAG1 p.C176F founder variant
Combined multi-omics, immune phenotyping, and repertoire analysis of BCR/TCR
Measured recombinase activity, cytokine/chemokine markers, autoantibodies, and CMV-specific immunity
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a clinically diverse cohort with the variant showing 25.8% wild-type recombinase activity and linked immune signatures across cellular and molecular readouts.
watch_item: Findings come from a rare, genetically enriched cohort, so the biomarkers and severity patterns may not generalize broadly without external validation.
paper_title: Multi-omics approach to map a clinically diverse large cohort with homozygous founder RAG1 p.C176F variant among Old Order Mennonites
